# Economists Raise US Inflation Forecasts as Iran War Drags On

US households are dealing with gasoline prices that have been hovering around $4 a gallon on average, Photographer: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg

By Mark Niquette and Dana Morgan

April 24, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC

Economists raised their estimates for US inflation and said they expect only one Federal Reserve interest-rate cut this year amid elevated energy costs sparked by the Iran war.

The personal consumption expenditures price index is now seen rising 3.6% in the second quarter from a year earlier, according to Bloomberg’s April survey of economists. That compares with the 3.3% estimate in the March survey.

# Inflation held sticky at 3% as U.S. headed into war with Iran, key Fed gauge shows 

 By metapress.net On Apr 22, 2026 

Core inflation held above the Federal Reserve’s target before the recent surge in energy prices, according to a key gauge released Thursday that offers the central bank a snapshot of conditions leading into the Iran war.

The core personal consumption expenditures price index, which excludes food and energy, rose a seasonally adjusted 3% in February, the Commerce Department reported. The all-items headline inflation measure increased 2.8%.

Both readings were in line with the Dow Jones consensus. The core annual inflation rate was 0.1 percentage point lower than in January while headline was unchanged.

On a monthly basis, both core and headline prices rose 0.4%, also meeting forecasts.

# US Inflation Hits 3.3% in March 2026: What to Know

 Written by: Malik Saaka

 April 23, 2026 

## Key Takeaways

- The March 2026 Consumer Price Index rose 3.3% year-over-year, the highest reading since May 2024.
- Prices rose 0.9% month-over-month, the biggest monthly gain since June 2022.
- Gasoline prices jumped 21.2% in a single month – the largest monthly surge since 1967.
- Core inflation (excluding food and energy) ticked up to 2.6% annually, showing broader price pressure.
- The report reduces the chances of Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026 and keeps pressure on household budgets.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics dropped an inflation bombshell on April 10, 2026. The headline Consumer Price Index surged to 3.3% on an annual basis in March, up from 2.4% in both January and February. One month of recent data shows the dilemma.

February inflation numbers under the key measure tracked by the Fed came in nearly a percentage point above the central bank’s 2% target. ## Compounding shocks to keep the Fed sidelined 

We expect a largely uneventful Fed meeting next week for a committee that is increasingly taking a backseat role – observing macroeconomic conditions and responding to them rather than steering them from the driver’s seat. In the face of compounding inflation shocks (a geopolitical event and a trade war), we expect that the Fed will stand pat and await additional data.
